# The Economy

## The grounded baseline

> status: ratified (D-0004, D-0026, D-0042)

Medieval economic underpinnings, strictly: muscle, wind, and water for power; walking
pace for information; iron dear enough that a plough is wealth. The technology mix is
deliberately time-blurred but never modern — oracle decks and tapestries exist, books
are rare and expensive, medicine has real concepts and crude instruments, and there is
no electricity or engine-power of any kind.

## Standardization against craft

> status: ratified (D-0042)

The signature economic violence of the ruling order: cheap, mass-made, deliberately
shoddy goods — the "amazon/mass cheap crap metaphor in medieval clothes" (authors'-room
phrasing only) — flooding out the human-scale crafts. The empire's stamped tools fail
by design and must be replaced from the empire's stores; the mended, the bespoke, and
the durable are taxed, licensed, or outlawed. Preserving dying crafts is thus both
cultural rescue and economic resistance ([[artifacts-and-memory]], [[professions]]).

## The widening lens

> status: ratified (D-0077)

A core storytelling device: how different communities' economies work is not
understood by the apprentice — and so not fully explained to the listener — until the
road teaches them. Each new region's economic rules arrive as lived surprise, additive
and enriching, never as lecture. The apprentice's education in survival arithmetic IS
the audience's tour of the world-system.

## Five local economies (session sketches)

> status: proposed

Worked examples awaiting ruling — each one a candidate "lesson" for the widening lens:

- **Scrip valleys**: keeps that pay in company tokens worthless one valley over —
  labor mobility abolished by currency itself; the apprentice's saved coins suddenly
  buying nothing.
- **The caloric standard**: dense foods (honey, butter, cured fat) taxed and hoarded
  because deep proof-work burns the body's stores — bread for muscles, famine for
  minds; a jar of honey worth more than a knife in the hidden markets.
- **The idle tax**: quotas measured as ceaseless output, so villages perform labor —
  wheels turned by hand in dry rivers — to keep their standing, working to appear
  working.
- **The gift-debt of the deep bogs**: beyond the empire's coin lies the old economy,
  where accepting a bowl of stew binds you by Frith unless balanced in kind — 
  generosity as a loaded instrument; the anchor slapping food from the apprentice's
  hand.
- **The rust market**: the underground economy of repair — illegal whetstones,
  solvent, files; a mended pot as contraband; the anchor's true wealth being his tools
  and his hands.

## Hedge-fairs

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The shadow-commons: illegal night markets at liminal places where the disenfranchised
trade by reciprocity — seed, iron, remedies, rumors, and the occasional saved theorem
on a vellum scrap. Where the trio goes to learn what officialdom will not say.

## The boundary contrast

> status: ratified (D-0140, D-0144, D-0156)

The empire builds in mortared walls of standardized finished stone, cut to one
measure at the quarries and set by gangs who need no eye for the ground. Such a wall
is the first false proof made solid ([[first-storehouse-lie]]): it declares the
ground it encloses to stand outside the web of reciprocity, and it holds the
declaration by force. Nothing crosses it — not the hare, not the freshet, not the
seed — and the land it severs sours, the debt seeping out around its foot as it once
seeped around the first storehouse. It is enclosure in a single object, and it is
keep-stamped work at the scale of a horizon: it displaces the fitted local wall-craft
the way a licensed tool displaces a trade.

The living hedge is its reclaimed opposite. A laid hedge is a boundary that still
lets the web pass, and it holds only because each generation re-lays it; left unlaid,
it gaps and the road it sheltered is lost. Where the wall promises the permanence of
needing no one, the hedge keeps the harder covenant of upkeep ([[cycles]],
[[wyrd-and-frith]]). Laid along a road as its wall, the same boundary that divides
becomes the way that connects: the empire's enclosure-fences re-pleached into the
people's shared roads (the Hedge Road, D-0139) — the master's barrier rewoven into
the path between communities.

The older dry-stone craft is the displaced native wall-work of the crag country
(D-0144): fitted by eye, stone answering stone, the same craft-dignity that lives in
the perfect unseen finish (D-0123) — and now displaced by the quarries' standard
units. It keeps an honest grey: a dry-stone wall still divides, and so the world
refuses any tidy reading of stone as evil and hedge as good; what the empire took
from the crags was not the wall but the craft of fitting it.

Where the wall must show its teeth, it does so procedurally: the checkpoint in
the wall — the queue, the pass, the bored clerk deciding who moves — is the
banal-fascism anchor's honest boundary expression, never spectacle (D-0156).
And dry-stone keeps its grey: a wall is a wall, even a beautiful one.
